row.evidence: Sprout's SCIM guides require "API permissions (to create API Tokens in Sprout)", and its API token article says "Your account must be on an Advanced plan to include API access."
row.notes: SCIM (Okta and Entra ID) went GA in September 2026; the Advanced plan gate is inferred because SCIM setup needs an API token and API access is Advanced-only ($399 vs Standard $199 per seat/month annual; monthly $249/$499). SSO (SAML only) is described as available to all customers, though an SSO FAQ says it needs an assigned CSM. Okta's OIN listing is still SAML/SWA only; Sprout's guide configures SCIM on that app with a bearer token. Deactivation keeps the account; Entra hard delete removes it. Public API is read-only for users (list active users). Essentials ($79) lacks collaboration features, so Standard is the team plan.

auth.token_source: Account and settings > Global Features > API > Generate API Token (needs API Permissions)

operations.notes: Okta's 'Update User Attributes' action is supported; the docs do not say whether updates arrive as PUT or PATCH.

deprovision.data_retained: Deactivated account is preserved (inactive, not deleted) and can be reactivated; Entra hard delete (after 30 days or manual permanent delete) fully removes the user, irreversibly.

custom.how: Sprout stores only first name, last name, email and username; title, department, manager, phoneNumbers, addresses and profileUrl are not supported.

roles.how: Group push: the pushed group displayName must match (case-insensitive) a Sprout Org Role or Profile Permission Set name; one Org Role and one PPS per user.

limitations.text: Only Okta and Microsoft Entra ID have SCIM setup guides.
Legacy roles are not supported; Org Roles and Profile Permission Sets must exist first.
Only one Org Role and one PPS per user via SCIM; two role-mapped groups cause a sync error.
Users with custom permissions cannot be SCIM-managed.
Provisioning fails when no seats are available.
Entra nested group membership is not provisioned.

scim.notes: SCIM went GA on 14 September 2026 for Okta and Entra ID. The SCIM Connector Base URL is shown in Settings > Authentication & Provisioning > Identity Provider Integrations; its pattern is not published. The plan gate is derived: setup needs a Sprout API token, and API access requires the Advanced plan. SCIM has Test (Validate) and Live modes.

rate_limits.text: 60 requests per minute; 250,000 requests per month

limitations.text: No create, update, deactivate or role endpoints for users; the API is read-only for users.

user_api.notes: The public API is for social analytics and publishing; its only user endpoint is a read-only list of active users.

okta.notes: OIN listing (last updated 2019) checks SAML and SWA only. Sprout's own guide configures SCIM on the installed Sprout Social app using the SCIM Connector Base URL and a bearer token.

entra.notes: Sprout's guide uses the existing Sprout Social enterprise app; no Microsoft Learn tutorial was found (sprout-social-tutorial 404).

google.notes: Sprout lists Google as a supported SAML IdP; no Google catalogue page checked.

onelogin.notes: Sprout lists OneLogin as a supported SAML IdP; OneLogin catalogue blocks bots.

conflicts.text: The SSO configuration article says self-service SSO is available to all customers; the SSO FAQ says it is not available for trial accounts or customers without an assigned CSM, and the pricing page lists 'Dedicated service for hassle-free SSO setup' only on Enterprise.
Okta's OIN page marks the Sprout Social app as SAML/SWA only, while Sprout's guide configures SCIM provisioning on that app.

searched: https://support.sproutsocial.com help-centre search API: scim, single sign-on, provisioning, okta, user management, API token, audit log, Just-in-time
open_questions: SCIM docs do not name a plan; the Advanced gate is inferred from the API-token requirement. Confirm whether Essentials-Professional customers can use SCIM.
SCIM version, base URL pattern, PUT vs PATCH, filtering, pagination and rate limits are not documented.
Docs do not say whether deactivation frees the seat or ends active sessions.
Entra gallery listing for Sprout Social not confirmed.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Account Owner role, or the Manage Single Sign-On permission + API permissions (to create API Tokens in Sprout)

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Go to Settings > Authentication & Provisioning>Identity Provider Integrations (tab) Select Enabled Via SCIM and click Start Configuring SCIM

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Authentication Mode should be HTTP Header and when you select that, paste in the API token you generated in Sprout in the Authorization : Bearer field.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Under Provisioning > To App, click Edit and enable: Create Users Update User Attributes Deactivate Users All three are required.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Sprout stores a limited set of user attributes — first name, last name, email, and username.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: When configuring Push Groups, you set the remote group name - this is the displayName Sprout receives and uses to look up the matching Org Role or Profile Permission Set.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Deactivate the user in Okta, or remove them from the Sprout app assignment. Sprout will lock or remove the user automatically — no action needed in Sprout.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Required Org Roles and Profile Permission Sets must exist in order for users to be provisioned with them, therefore these should be set up first. Legacy roles are not supported.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: Keep in mind that only one Org Role and one PPS can be assigned to a user via SCIM. Assigning a user to two groups that both map to a role (or both map to a PPS) will cause a sync error.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: If someone has custom permissions set up in Sprout (permissions outside the standard Roles and Permission Sets), they should not be added to any Okta or Entra group that's mapped to Sprout. Doing so will cause a sync error.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: SCIM has two modes: Validate and Live.

citations.title: Configuring SCIM Provisioning with Okta
citations.quote: How do I switch from JIT provisioning to SCIM? Go to Settings > Authentication & Provisioning in Sprout, disable JIT, and follow the SCIM setup steps above.
